svg.title: KDA fixed state versus production and public MLA caches
svg.desc: A portrait comparison for one K3 layer. KDA has one fixed 96 by 128 by 128 recurrent state. Production MLA adds a 576-value payload per token. The public Hugging Face reference expands each token to 96 by 192 key values plus 96 by 128 value values before caching, or 30,720 values per token.
svg.text: What one layer keeps during decode
Fixed sequence state and per-token cache are different bargains.
KDA · FIXED WITH SEQUENCE LENGTH
One recurrent matrix per head summarizes the whole prefix.
After T tokens: still 1,572,864 values in this layer.
Tradeoff: bounded state, but arbitrary old tokens are not separate.
PRODUCTION MLA
COMPRESSED PAYLOAD PER TOKEN
512 latent + 64 shared key = 576 values / token
Projection absorption keeps this compressed payload in cache.
After T tokens: 576T cached values in this layer
Tradeoff: token entries remain addressable, so storage grows with T.
PUBLIC HF PYTHON
EXPANDED KEY/VALUE CACHE PER TOKEN
= 30,720 cached values / token
Reference code expands per-head K/V before cache update.
After T tokens: 30,720T cached values in this layer
Readable inference code; not the production latent-cache footprint.
KDA compresses across tokens.
Production MLA compresses within each token.
